correctness.rationale: Oeding supplies the exact projective tensor model and its (SL(2)^n) semidirect S_n invariance. The powers-of-two diagonal cocharacter separates all 2^n tensor-coordinate weights, so the ambient fixed locus is finite and exactly coordinate. Every coordinate point belongs to Z_n: group invariance moves the empty-subset point through all coordinates, and independently the explicit diagonal degeneration has exponent gap |I\J|+|J\I|, giving a unique limiting coordinate. Therefore the fixed locus of Z_n has exactly 2^n points. Algebraic C* localization of compactly supported Euler characteristic applies without smoothness, and projectivity gives ordinary Euler characteristic. Additivity then gives zero compactly supported Euler characteristic for the complement. The packaged checker replays the weight separation and degeneration exponents on broad finite ranges, but those finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Z_n is a natural and extensively studied algebraic variety arising from the symmetric principal-minor assignment problem, with applications recorded in probability, statistical physics, spectral graph theory, and tensor geometry. Its dimension grows quadratically, binom(n+1,2), while its ambient projective dimension grows exponentially, 2^n-1, so equality of its Euler characteristic with the ambient value 2^n is a non-obvious global statement. The formula is uniform for every n>=4, identifies the entire compactly supported Euler characteristic of the complement as zero, and isolates a clean topological consequence of the large SL(2)^n symmetry. This is a canonical invariant of a literature-standard family rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
